programs.title: KOLs and other ways to connect cultures
programs.desc: In what ways can KOLs better use their power in an age where a single video can reach millions? Tune in to #GlobalSouthNextGen: Voices and Visions, and check out the stories of two KOLs from Ghana and Indonesia who use their creativity, empathy, and the shared desire to make people understand each other a little better.

programs.title: Start small, dream big: Young entrepreneurs shape our future
programs.desc: Tune in to #GlobalSouthNextGen: Voices and Visions! Hear the incredible stories of the young entrepreneurs who are doing things differently. One connects beauty services with people in need, while the other turns waste into sustainable solutions, all while lifting up their communities. Don’t you miss this!

programs.title: Discovering Guizhou: Miao culture extravaganza
programs.desc: What do spicy peppers, handmade guitars, and green cities have in common? Guizhou. In our new on-the-ground mini-series ChinaHorizons, we invite you to join our trip to Guizhou province. For the first stop, we record our podcast in a traditional Miao people's village cluster to appreciate diversified cultures, intangible cultural heritage items and delicious local cuisines.

programs.title: China's rural CEO experiment: How a Dai village is reinventing itself
programs.desc: During the Dai New Year, CGTN reporter Lincoln Humphries visited Manluanzhan, a traditional Dai village near China's southwestern border in Yunnan Province. There, "sleeping" assets are being awakened: an abandoned water tower has been turned into a café, and traditional Dai houses have been expanded to offer new types of homestays. At the center of this experiment is an unusual figure — a rural CEO who helps balance economic development with the Dai community's traditions as the village charts its own path forward. In this episode of #BizFocus, Lincoln Humphries shows how a village in Xishuangbanna brings fresh vitality and authentic traditions together.

programs.title: China's Kungfu theme park: A wild ride back in time
programs.desc: At Wansuishan Martial Arts City in central China’s Kaifeng, Henan Province, you’re not just a visitor - you’re part of the story. Every segment in the park is part of an immersive experience rooted in Chinese martial arts and traditional culture. From live matchmaking shows to iron flower performances, from Song Dynasty streets to interactive stages, this uniquely Chinese theme park – with not even one roller coaster or scary ride – was able to record over 24 million visits in 2025.

programs.title: New consumption scenes: Exploring Suzhou's lotus market with a foreign vlogger
programs.desc: Cherry Qiu and foreign vlogger Wang Dehua visited the famous Taohuawu Lotus Market in Suzhou, and savored the Su‑style lifestyle. This livestream showcases how traditional Chinese culture thrives in modern consumption scenarios, and how Suzhou leverages its distinctive cultural resources to create new inbound‑tourism experiences marked by greater interactivity, immersive engagement and international appeal.

programs.title: RAZOR: Wooden Windmills
programs.desc: As we shift to green energy, it's important to ask - how green is the infrastructure itself? Take wind power: a typical onshore turbine needs around 480 tonnes of steel, and producing just one tonne of steel or cement releases up to two tonnes of CO2. In Sweden, engineers at Modvion are tackling this problem by building wind turbine towers out of wood. RAZOR meets the team behind Wind of Change, one of the tallest wooden towers in the world. Co-founder David Olivegren got the idea while building a boat, while CEO Otto Lundman explains how sustainably sourced wood is turned into strong, lightweight Laminated Veneer Lumber (LVL). CFO Maria-Lina Hedlund shares how the company aims to scale in a competitive green energy market.

programs.title: Walk Again: A New Hope for Paralysis Recovery
programs.desc: A groundbreaking medical technology in China is offering new hope to people with paralysis. In Hangzhou, doctors and engineers at Second Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University School of Medicine have developed a closed-loop spinal cord neural interface that helps reconnect signals between the brain and muscles, allowing patients with spinal cord injuries to stand and walk again. This episode follows patients and doctors through a pioneering surgery and the long road to recovery - exploring whether technology can help the human body walk again.

programs.title: Rate Decision Week in Focus
programs.desc: The Fed has resumed rate hikes for the first time in three years, while the Bank of Japan is set to make its next move. With energy prices elevated and inflation pressures persisting, central banks are turning more hawkish. Will tightening continue? And what does it mean for the dollar, yen, renminbi, Treasuries and gold? This week on BizTalk, we take a closer look at the new global rate cycle and its market impact.#BizTalk

programs.title: Vive La Tech: Approaching the limits of temperature measurement
programs.desc: In this episode of CGTN's special program "Vive La Tech," we dive into the "frozen world". In low-temperature metrology, scientists created the world's most precise temperature measuring device, from 5 to 24.5 kelvin, providing a source for all thermometers around the world. Join CGTN reporter Yang Zhao to explore how such an innovative partnership can open new doors for fundamental science.

programs.title: Vive la Tech: Climate change is changing French wine
programs.desc: CGTN's new special program "Vive La Tech" focuses on some of the coolest science collaborations between China and France. In this episode, we shift our attention to climate change and the grape at risk. Follow our reporter Yang Zhao into the vineyards.

programs.title: Meet China: Starting Green, Reaching the Future
programs.desc: In this episode of Meet China, wind becomes more than a natural force—it powers a greener future across China and Europe. A piece of fabric reveals how Chinese innovation is reshaping global perceptions of manufacturing. Ancient ruins in central China are reimagined as immersive cultural experiences, turning heritage into living memory. And in Laos, Chinese agricultural expertise is helping farmers unlock higher yields and new opportunities. From energy and textiles to tourism and farming, this episode shows how innovation is renewing tradition and connecting futures across borders.

programs.title: Farmed with China: Malaysia's rice has a secret superpower
programs.desc: Despite its fertile tropical landscape, Malaysia produces only around two-thirds of the rice it needs. Chinese ratoon rice technology is now being applied to lift yields and enhance food security—unlocking new potential for tropical farming. Discover more in CGTN's special series #FarmedwithChina. #Chinavsionary

programs.title: Farmed with China: Vietnam's food trade levels up
programs.desc: How is Vietnam's cassava industry reaching global markets? With technical support and cross-border cooperation with China, one crop is moving up the value chain — from local farms to international supply chains.

programs.title: Farmed with China: Thailand's farms go high-tech
programs.desc: As labor grows scarce, how can the land still yield abundant harvests? China-Thailand cooperation is providing solutions: machines for farmers, jobs in factories, and training for young agricultural engineers. Technology is more than equipment — it brings efficiency and hope.

programs.title: Cambodia's rice prawn=making more money!
programs.desc: Rice and prawn grow better together. Prawn loosens the soil and control pests, while rice cleans and oxygenates the water. One field, two harvests. A team from Shanghai Ocean University brought this eco-farming model to Cambodia, helping turn rice paddies into new sources of income.

programs.title: Laos farmers hack one season into many
programs.desc: Laos is transforming traditional agriculture into a modern locally-adapted system with the cooperation of China, applying benefits from a decade of seed innovation as well as the domestic development of potash resources. Alongside China-Laos Railway strengthening the supply chain, grain production is also gaining a stronger foundation. Explore the story in CGTN's special series Farmed With China.

programs.title: The AI revolution is here - but are we ready for what comes next?
programs.desc: In this special joint episode of World Economic Forum and CGTN, hosts Robin Pomeroy from World Economic Forum and Guan Xin, CGTN Anchor, sit down with Professor Arun Sundararajan of New York University's Stern School of Business, a member of the WEF AI Governance Alliance and author of The Sharing Economy. They dive into the most pressing questions about artificial intelligence. From the future of employment to the deepening divide over AI governance and technological sovereignty, this conversation brings together perspectives from the US, China, and the global stage on how AI is reshaping economies, societies, and geopolitics.
